sites.evidence_type: published tolerance of a different insertion (transposon, FP fusion)
sites.functional_impact_measured: RGD cluster nucleation confirmed at 15 and 60 min; live-cell adhesion assembly and dissociation from RGD clusters observed — integrin ligand-binding and adhesion dynamics preserved.
sites.rationale: ITGB6 is a Type I transmembrane protein with a single extracellular N-terminus (mature residue 22) and an intracellular C-terminus; an EGFP tag confirmed on the cell surface can only reside at the N-terminal position after signal-peptide cleavage. Python lookup confirms residue 21 = G (last SP residue) and residue 22 = G (first mature extracellular residue), placing the junction at insert_after_residue = 21. The ectodomain is 688 residues from the junction to the TM boundary, far exceeding the ≥3-residue clearance requirement. RGD cluster nucleation and adhesion assembly in live cells constitute a functional readout of integrin–ligand engagement. Full-length EGFP-tagged integrin β6 expressed in CHO-B2 cells; surface display confirmed by RGD cluster nucleation at 15 and 60 min (L2) and live-cell imaging of adhesion assembly and dissociation from RGD clusters (L3). ITGB6 is a Type I single-pass protein (extracellular 22–709, TM 710–730, intracellular 731–788); the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage at residue 21.

sources.claim: A) EGFP‐tagged integrin β6, β5, and β3 expressed in CHO‐B2 cells nucleate RGD clusters in 15 and 60‐min.

literature_notes: L1 (PMC8932414) was examined and disqualified: the construct spans aa22–709 only (the ectodomain), with a C-terminal coiled coil replacing the TM domain; it is a soluble ectodomain reagent, not a membrane-anchored full-length protein, and therefore does not qualify per the rules. L2 and L3 both report the same EGFP-tagged β6 construct in CHO-B2 cells; L2 is cited as the primary supporting clip, with L3 providing corroborating live-cell functional evidence. No residue or loop is named in either L2 or L3, but because ITGB6 is a Type I single-pass protein with exactly one extracellular terminus (the mature N-terminus after SP cleavage), the position is unambiguously topology-derived at insert_after_residue = 21. Confidence is medium rather than high because no residue is explicitly named in the source papers.
